title: Carmelo Anthony calls out Ravens' Marlon Humphrey after controversial Baltimore 'criminals' comment - CBS Sports
description: Anthony spent his formative years growing up in Baltimore and wasn't going to let Humphrey's comments slide
body:
Anthony spent his formative years growing up in Baltimore and wasn't going to let Humphrey's comments slide
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:24 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Among sports fans, Carmelo Anthony is perhaps most synonymous with New York -- both upstate from his incredible year at Syracuse and in New York City, where he starred for the Knicks. But Anthony was raised in Baltimore and is extremely proud of his roots. So when Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey made headlines this week when he said that the thing the city of Baltimore was best at creating was "criminals," Anthony felt compelled to respond. Humphrey was admonished by the Ravens, which sent him home for the week and will hold him out on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers. He also received scathing responses from Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott and many other prominent Baltimore figures. Anthony joined that group on Friday with an Instagram post that called on Humphrey to go beyond the apology he issued earlier in the week. Anthony wants Humphrey to join him, Scott, and others in the community to find ways to lead by example. 

I've been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn't a talking point to me. It's in my blood. I came up on Myrtle Avenue in West Baltimore. I saw what this city can take fro you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. I've heard every joke and every headline my whole life. So when one of our own stands on our name and says the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it'll get cut out, that doesn't get cut out for me. It doesn't get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn't get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner. And it doesn't get cut out for the man who did his time, came home, and is fighting every day to be seen as more than his worst moment. Marlon, I see the apology. I'll take it, man to man. But Baltimore has been apologized to its whole life. Apologies don't build anything. Presence does. I put my time, energy and resources in Baltimore because I want kids to have somebody who believe in them. That's the job when you wear this city on your chest. You don't get to rep Baltimore on Sundays and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday. So let me tell you what Baltimore makes. We make fighters. We make builders. We make people who were counted out from the day they were born and showed up anyway. We make teachers who buy supplies out of their own pockets, coaches who become fathers, artists the whole world copies, and returning citizens who turn their pain into purpose. We make Olympians, Hall of Famers, legends. We make ME. We make Tank Davis. The Mayor opened a door. Walk through it. And when you do, call me. I'll meet you there. Let's sit with these young boys together and let them hear from two men who wear this city that they are not what anybody says they are. Baltimore doesn't make criminals. Baltimore makes the ones who make it out. And the ones who come back. #B-MORE. PEACE, CHAMPThe overwhelming response to Humphrey's comments in Baltimore has been to highlight the incredible work being done by leaders to improve conditions, decrease violence, and provide mentorship and guidance to young people in the city. 
Anthony echoed the mayor's invitation to join in that work in the community and offered to be there right alongside him.

title: Anatomy of Ohio State's 2026 meltdown: How Buckeyes went from preseason No. 1 to elimination from CFP race - CBS Sports
description: A devastating injury to Julian Sayin, fourth-quarter collapses and questionable staff moves derailed a national c
body:
A devastating injury to Julian Sayin, fourth-quarter collapses and questionable staff moves derailed a national championship favorite and sparked the program's worst collapse since 2011
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A season that started with national championship aspirations and a preseason No. 1 ranking could end with a trip to the Citrus Bowl.No. 14 Ohio State's faint playoff hopes were officially extinguished Saturday when Nebraska broke a decade-long losing streak and finally got a win over a top-25 opponent. Ecstatic Nebraska fans rushed the field to celebrate the Cornhuskers' 31-28 win over the Buckeyes.It is the first time since 2011 that Ohio State has lost consecutive road games. In case you forgot, 2011 was the Luke Fickell interim 6-6 season that preceded the Urban Meyer era. It's not a stretch to say this 2026 season is the worst in 15 years, and one could argue it's even worse than 2011 given the expectations and talent on the roster. Poor Jeremiah Smith's talent is being wasted on the most disappointing Ohio State team in decades. How did Ohio State get here? Here's a look at the Buckeyes' drop to rock bottom. 
Winter 2026Ryan Day made two key decisions last winter that had the potential to significantly impact the Buckeyes' season.First, Day hired former Atlanta Falcons head coach Arthur Smith as his offensive coordinator. On paper, it felt like a potential upgrade over the outgoing Brian Hartline, who left to become South Florida's head coach. Under Hartline, Ohio State's offense was efficient but seemed to be missing some of the explosiveness from the previous season. Day even took over play-calling responsibilities late in the season when Hartline was balancing two jobs. Smith, who had been the Pittsburgh Steelers' offensive coordinator the previous season, was expected to improve the run game.Next, Ohio State retained defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, who had received some interest in returning to the NFL. Ohio State's defense flourished in Year 1 with Patricia, finishing No. 1 in total defense and scoring defense (only 9.3 points allowed per game). Ohio State rewarded Patricia, making him the highest-paid assistant coach in college football. 
Collapse in AustinOhio State led No. 4 Texas, 23-3, in the fourth quarter and … lost.It was a historic collapse for the Buckeyes on Sept. 12 in Austin. Texas' fourth-quarter comeback to win 24-23 was the largest against a No. 1-ranked team in history. It had the potential to be the kind of marquee win that Ohio State could hold up if anyone attacked its playoff resume. To beat a playoff-caliber team like Texas on the road would have been ginormous. Instead, it was a what-could-have-been result that elicited early questions about Arthur Smith after Ohio State's late-game conservative play-calling blew up in its face. Still, it felt too early to panic about a team that was considered to be one of, if not the, most talented teams in the country. As long as Ohio State took care of business in Big Ten play, it'd be fine. 
Won the battle, lost the war The definition of a pyrrhic victory for the Buckeyes. Ohio State held off Indiana, 19-15, on Oct. 17 in a rematch of last year's Big Ten Championship Game. It gave Ohio State a resume-defining win, but the bigger news was the injury star quarterback Julian Sayin suffered late in the game. Sayin fractured his right elbow, according to reports, and was later ruled out indefinitely. Ohio State would never recover from the loss of Sayin, a Heisman Trophy finalist in 2025, and didn't have a viable backup option to keep the offense humming. Sayin never got the credit he deserved as Ohio State's quarterback, as critics believed he was more a product of the surrounding talent than what he could do himself. And while there's no question having Jeremiah Smith to throw the ball to downfield was supremely helpful, the impact of Sayin's absence should make fans realize how good they had it. No treat against TrojansIt was a Halloween debacle for the Buckeyes against a desperate USC team looking for a big win. It was the first real test of how Ohio State would look without Sayin, and the Buckeyes failed. 
True freshman Luke Fahey wasn't bad against the Trojans, but the offense clearly took a step back. In its 30-18 loss to USC, Ohio State ended up with three field goals on its first five offensive drives despite having the ball on the Trojans' 1-yard line on one of those drives. Perhaps even more concerning was how bad the defense looked at times. USC capitalized on a defensive breakdown for a 69-yard touchdown in the first minute of the game. By the middle of the third quarter, USC had a 27-9 lead it would never relinquish. It would be too simplistic  -- and perhaps unfair -- to say that the defense stopped playing as well because it didn't believe in Fahey the way it did Sayin, but it is strange how much worse Matt Patricia's group seemed to look, from an effort and execution standpoint, post-Sayin injury. There was hope that Ohio State had enough talent to survive the loss of Sayin. The poor effort against USC cast a lot of doubt on that. 
Fake punt breaks OSUOregon's gutsy (and successful) fake punt call in the second quarter seemed to break an Ohio State team that had raced out to a 14-0 lead.It was stunning to see Ohio State just completely collapse afterward in what turned into a 41-28 loss to the Ducks that severely damaged the Buckeyes' playoff hopes. This was the last-stand type of game for Ohio State, a must-win home game against a team that had also lost its own star quarterback (Dante Moore) to an injury this season. And for a quarter-and-a-half, Ohio State looked the part. But in what has proven to be a defining characteristic of this Ohio State team, when it faces real adversity, it crumbles. It happened against Texas, and it happened again against Oregon. At one point, Oregon scored 38 consecutive points, the first time since 1999 the Buckeyes gave up that many points in a row. 
"We didn't expect any of this to happen," Day said. The loss prompted a series of questions, from possible staff changes to why Ohio State hasn't been better at developing quarterbacks. Most importantly, all the goodwill Ryan Day collected from the 2024 title run seemed to dissipate with the loss. Disaster seasonSome of us, including this College Football Playoff prognosticator, already thought Ohio State's playoff hopes should be dead. But after a win over Northwestern and chaos engulfing the teams ranked above them, the Buckeyes moved all the way up to No. 14 in this week's CFP Rankings. It was still a long shot, but one couldn't definitively rule Ohio State out in case a few of the higher-ranked teams lost in the final weeks of the season.Nebraska ended that notion once and for all. The Cornhuskers ended a 31-game losing streak against ranked opponents when they beat the Buckeyes. The loss drops Ohio State to 7-4, its worst record since 2011. Ryan Day is now 7-6 in his last 13 games as Ohio State's head coach. 
The defense again struggled, especially early as Nebraska built a 21-7 lead. When it badly needed a stop late in the game, it could not stop Cornhuskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea from getting the first down. Colandrea finished with four total touchdowns (3 passing, 1 rushing) and delivered the final nail in the coffin for Ohio State's season."We're not gonna win many games if we're giving up 31 points and only getting two stops in the whole game," Day said afterward. As bleak as it felt for Day and Ohio State after a shocking 2024 loss to Michigan, this is worse. And it has the potential to get even uglier if Ohio State can't beat a bad Michigan team next week in The Game.

schema.headline: Anatomy of Ohio State's 2026 meltdown: How Buckeyes went from preseason No. 1 to elimination from CFP race - CBS Sports

title: A.J. Ewing, Mets agree to eight-year, $95 million extension after standout rookie season, per reports - CBS Sports
description: Ewing cracked the top 10 in the National League Rookie of the Year voting last season
body:
Ewing cracked the top 10 in the National League Rookie of the Year voting last season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The New York Mets and center fielder A.J. Ewing have agreed to an eight-year contract extension, SNY reports. The deal will pay Ewing a guaranteed $95 million and includes an option for a ninth year, according to The Athletic. The extension will run through the 2034 season and, if the option is exercised, through 2035. 
Ewing, 22, is coming off a 2026 rookie campaign in which he batted .252/.324/.376 (97 OPS+) with 11 home runs and 25 stolen bases in 120 games for the Mets. Additionally, Ewing graded out as a pronounced defensive asset in center field according to the eye test and fielding metrics. His overall WAR of 3.1 this past season helped him crack the top 10 in the National League Rookie of the Year vote. The Mets originally selected Ewing in the fourth round of the 2023 draft out of an Ohio high school. Following a strong campaign at Double-A and Triple-A in 2025, Ewing entered the 2026 season as a consensus top-100 prospect in baseball. In terms of overall value, he's already begun living up to those expectations. The extension expresses confidence on the club's side that Ewing will continue to be a valuable core contributor for years to come. Even if the bat doesn't develop as hoped, Ewing's foundation of excellent defense at an up-the-middle position provides him a high floor of worth over the long term. He's part of an emerging core of young Mets talent that also includes starting pitcher Nolan McLean and Ewing's fellow outfielder Carson Benge, who both finished ahead of Ewing in that Rookie of the Year balloting. As well, catcher Francisco Alvarez is still just 25 years old. 
No matter what happens with the Mets' high ambitions on the free-agent market, Ewing will be an essential part of the Mets' efforts to move beyond the disappointments of 2026. This past season, the Mets finished 14 games below .500 and in last place in the NL East despite having the league's highest Opening Day payroll.

title: Harry Kane ankle surgery: Why Bayern Munich may not have squad depth to withstand months without star striker - CBS Sports
description: Kane is expected to be sidelined for several months as Vincent Kompany faces a full-blown crisis with no true bac
body:
Kane is expected to be sidelined for several months as Vincent Kompany faces a full-blown crisis with no true backup striker
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Bayern Munich's depth was already pushed to the limit, but Friday's 1-1 draw with Koln may have broken Vincent Kompany's side. Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane lasted only 20 minutes before exiting with what the club is calling a "syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle," which required surgery overnight and will keep him sidelined "for months," according to sporting director Max Eberl.  "Harry Kane underwent successful surgery overnight after tearing his left ankle ligament in yesterday's home match against 1. FC Köln. The 33-year-old will now begin his rehab," Bayern said in a statement.  
Losing Kane alone is a significant blow to the Bavarians after they failed to replace Nicolas Jackson when his loan ended, but the injuries didn't stop there. Michael Olise was also withdrawn at halftime and left the stadium on crutches. This led to a match in which Bayern put only one shot on target against a side just above the relegation zone, showing this is a problem of their own creation in the transfer market. Coming into the season without a viable backup for an aging Kane would eventually hurt Bayern, and Kompany now needs to oversee a worst-case scenario. Luis Diaz and Ismael Saibari were already out with injuries, and when Kane went down, Thomas Bischof had to come in for him instead of a like-for-like striker. Even with Jamal Musiala's neurological issues, the players they do have aren't able to perform at their best. 
Already in an actual title race in the Bundesliga with Borussia Dortmund, these are the kinds of setbacks that can lead to a new German champion for the first time since Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24, and even they had to go undefeated to accomplish that feat, while this season could be Bayern's own undoing. They've been one of the top sides in the world when healthy, but as it is, this side will struggle in Champions League play, where they'll travel to face Lille. Precariously in 13th place in the Champions League league phase, Bayern won't fall out of the top 24 without Kane, but it could get close to something that they should be concerned about. Even missing out on the top eight and needing to play additional games is something that Bayern won't want to deal with, considering this injury crisis. Being a backup to Kane is a thankless task, as it's hard to get game time and you're also compared to one of the best players in the world, but it's still a multifaceted failure for Bayern to not have one. Real Madrid were able to recruit post-prime players to back up Karim Benzema, and now Kylian Mbappe has a backup from the academy. There's no reason that a club of Bayern's stature shouldn't be able to do the same, but here we are in the same position they constantly find themselves in. 
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Depth issues have held Bayern back from claiming a Champions League title in recent years. Kane winning the Ballon d'Or solidified that the starting XI is more than good enough to lift Europe's most coveted club trophy, and the difference between this side and the 2020 one that won the Champions League is their lack of depth.  
It's a strange situation with Musiala that isn't being handled well, with board members open to selling him, and it doesn't help the club's overall trajectory. Bayern will need to shake things up in January, but these issues began long before now, and to return to the top of the global game, they need to change the way they do things.

title: MLB rumors: Logan Webb trade possible for Giants, Freddy Peralta market picking up steam, more - CBS Sports
description: Here are the latest news and rumors in the MLB offseason on Saturday, Nov. 21
body:
Here are the latest news and rumors in the MLB offseason on Saturday, Nov. 21
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:03 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples. Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Saturday's supply just below. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Logan Webb trade a possibility for Giants
Will the San Francisco Giants trade their ace this offseason? That's a reasonable question to ask now that FanSided is reporting that the Giants are open to trade discussions regarding veteran right-hander Logan Webb. No doubt, Webb would be a coveted presence on the offseason market. Webb, who just recently turned 30, endured a bit of a down 2026 on the run-prevention front, but the overall body of work remains very strong. For his career, the three-time All-Star has a career ERA+ of 115 with three top-10 finishes in the American League Cy Young vote. In three of the past four seasons, he's topped 200 innings. 
Webb is under contract through 2028, and that extra year of team control makes him even more of an alluring trade target for contenders in need of rotation upgrades. Freddy Peralta market picking up steam
Freddy Peralta, who'll be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is one of the strongest free-agent starting pitchers on the market not named Tarik Skubal. As such, there's healthy interest in his services. The Tampa Bay Rays, the Chicago White Sox, the San Diego Padres, the Toronto Blue Jays, and two presently unknown clubs all have significant interest in signing Peralta, the Athletic reports. Peralta, coming off three straight seasons for the Milwaukee Brewers in which he topped 30 starts and 200 strikeouts, wasn't himself with the New York Mets for the first half-plus of 2027. However, after a deadline trade to the Rays, he made some adjustments and re-established himself as a highly useful starter. The market's going to reflect his rediscovered form. 
Itoh visits ChicagoRight-hander Hiromi Itoh, who's seeking to make the leap from Japan to MLB, was recently in Chicago to visit the Cubs or the White Sox, ESPN reports. Both Windy City squads are in need of pitching help, and Itoh would certainly help them on that front. The 29-year-old Itoh ranked 26th on CBS Sports' offseason list of the top free agents in the current class. Here's part of our write-up: "A down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons. He's seen as a crafty back-end starter in MLB, or perhaps even a reliever (Itoh sat 96 mph out of the bullpen in the World Baseball Classic). The Hokkaido Nippon Ham Fighters are expected to post Itoh, who turned 29 in August, this winter."The Cubs have a lot of uncertainty in the rotation, while the White Sox still need help even after adding Dustin May this offseason. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mets getting calls on Vientos
The New York Mets retained the services of first baseman Mark Vientos leading up to the recent non-tender deadline despite his pattern of decline over the last two seasons. Now, Vientos could be on the move. The soon-to-be 27-year-old has been the subject of trade inquiries, The Athletic reports. 
While Vientos is coming off a highly disappointing 2026 season, he still has power potential and in his semi-recent past a 2024 campaign in which he hit 27 home runs in 111 games. All of that makes Vientos a fairly compelling change-of-scenery possibility, and the Mets may seek to make that happen this winter.

title: Where to watch Michigan vs. UCLA: TV channel, stream, odds, spread, prediction, pick - CBS Sports
description: The unbeaten Bruins can clinch a Big Ten title game berth, but the struggling Wolverines have a clear path to sho
body:
The unbeaten Bruins can clinch a Big Ten title game berth, but the struggling Wolverines have a clear path to shock their new conference rival if they protect the football
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Michigan has fallen so far under Kyle Whittingham that the all-time winningest program in college football has been reduced to being a home underdog against a UCLA program that won three games last season. The No. 4 Bruins are arriving for their first game at Michigan Stadium since 1996 on Saturday in prime position to reach the Big Ten Championship Game and College Football Playoff.The Wolverines team hosting them is scraping rock bottom after falling to 5-5 with a 31-7 loss at Oregon last week. It's a jarring backdrop for the first battle between these teams as Big Ten foes. At 10-0 (7-0 Big Ten), the Bruins are one win away from reaching 11 victories for the first time in program history. Just three years removed from a national championship, Michigan may be on the cusp of yet another coaching change.Lauded as a stabilizing hire amid a tumultuous ending to Sherrone Moore's tenure last year, Whittingham has presided over a disaster. Michigan ranks 131st of 138 FBS teams in total offense, averaging just 300.9 yards per game.While the Wolverines have quickly reached dire straits under Whittingham, 66, they can play the role of spoiler over the season's final two weeks. Handing UCLA its first loss and/or upsetting rival Ohio State to close the season would bring some morsel of satisfaction to what has been a painful 2026 slog in Ann Arbor.
Where to watch Michigan vs. UCLA liveDate: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ETLocation: Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, MichiganTV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports AppStreaming on Paramount+ PremiumMichigan vs. UCLA: Need to know  What's at stake for UCLA: Despite its 10-0 record, UCLA is still not a lock for the College Football Playoff. The Bruins' relative lack of marquee victories means they need to win at least one of their final two regular-season games to have a solid at-large case. The CBS Sports CFP Forecaster gives UCLA an 86.1% chance of making the field with a win over the Wolverines. A win would also lock up a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game for the Bruins, who close the regular season against crosstown rival USC next week.
Can Wayne Knight break free?: Wayne Knight rattled off three straight 100-plus yard rushing performances during UCLA's first three Big Ten victories. But in the past five games, the James Madison transfer has eclipsed the century mark just once. Last week's 22-14 win over Illinois marked his first game this season without either a rushing or receiving touchdown. After averaging 253.2 rushing yards per game on 6.1 yards per attempt in their first five games, the Bruins have averaged just 152.2 yards per game on 4.1 yards per attempt over their last five. If there's one thing Michigan does reasonably well, it's defend the run. Opponents are averaging just 103.1 yards per game on the ground against the Wolverines.Ongoing quarterback battle: With two games left in the regular season, there still isn't an established starting quarterback at Michigan. It's been that kind of season for the Wolverines, who played both Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr in last week's loss to Oregon. Interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding boiled this week's competition between the two signal-callers down to ball security. "Are you going to necessarily have an epiphany that in Week 11 the kid can do this particular thing?" Harding said. "I would not say that that's the case, but I think what you can evaluate in practice this week is who's valuing the importance of having the football at the end of the play. That honestly is the main piece in the evaluation is who can take care of the football." 
Michigan vs. UCLA prediction, picksOnly four FBS teams have committed more turnovers than Michigan, which has coughed up the football 19 times, leading to a -10 turnover margin. UCLA leads the nation in turnovers forced with 30. But what happens if the turnover luck shifts? The Wolverines have edged quality foes Oklahoma and Penn State by winning the turnover battle, and they took Indiana to overtime while winning it 2-1. If Michigan simply takes care of the football, it can beat a UCLA team that hasn't been running it effectively recently. Look for the Wolverines to produce an inspired effort in their home finale and spring an upset on the unbeaten Bruins.  Pick: Michigan SU

Kiffin heads back to Neyland Stadium searching for a signature victory as the ninth-ranked Volunteers lean on a dominant defense and running back DeSean Bishop

The Tigers moved to 6-4 in Lane Kiffin's first season after losing a heartbreaker against Texas 22-21 last week. Tennessee has been steady since making a quarterback change to George MacIntyre, winning five of its last six games. The Volunteers pulled away from Texas A&M in a 22-7 victory, led by a dominant defensive performance in College Station. LSU and Tennessee have not played since 2022, a 40-13 dominant for the Volunteers in Baton Rouge. Before that, the Tigers won five straight dating back to 2006. This is the first trip back to Knoxville for Kiffin since the famous 31-26 Ole Miss win in 2021 that led to Kiffin being pelted by golf balls and mustard bottles. Where to watch LSU vs. Tennessee liveDate: Saturday, Nov. 21 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ETLocation: Neyland Stadium -- Knoxville, TennesseeTV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  LSU vs. Tennessee: Need to know  Bishop's rise: Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop turned down Power Four offers to walk on at his hometown program. Now, he's emerged as one of the best in the nation. The junior is rushing for 1,163 yards and 13 touchdowns to power the Volunteers, including 97 or more yards in six straight games. 
Disappointing debut: Kiffin was hired at LSU in one of the biggest coaching decisions of the past several years. In Year 1, the results have been decidedly mixed. The Tigers sit at a paltry 6-4, including 0-4 against CFP-ranked opponents. LSU could desperately use even a single meaningful victory to build some momentum heading into 2027. Passing game woes: Tennessee started the year with freshman Faizon Brandon before handing the keys to George MacIntyre, but neither has provided much dynamism. The Volunteers rank No. 123 nationally in passing offense, mustering only 7.1 yards per attempt. Making matters worse, top receiver Mike Matthews is likely out for the season with a knee injury suffered against Texas A&M. That's bad news going against LSU's strong passing defense.   LSU vs. Tennessee prediction, picks  Expect a defensive struggle when Tennessee and LSU play in Knoxville. Neither quarterback has been consistent against great competition, and the defenses have shut down even elite opponents. That said, if you're giving me points for Tennessee in Neyland, I'm taking them. Pick: Tennessee +1.5

title: LOOK: Army trolls Navy before Midshipmen's game against Memphis by rearranging 'GO ARMY' seats - CBS Sports
description: Cadets managed to get into Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium and leave their mark
body:
Cadets managed to get into Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium and leave their mark
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:03 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Continuing the history of trolling one another prior to next month's end-of-season rivalry bout, Army one-upped Navy on Saturday after several cadets entered Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium and left a gift for the Midshipmen.According to The Athletic, Army cadets rearranged the usual "GO NAVY" seats in the upper deck at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium early Saturday morning before kickoff against Memphis.A Navy spokesperson told The Athletic that security cameras recorded cadets in uniform around 1 a.m. and that they managed to move the bolted-down chairbacks over the next several hours. More than a dozen Navy staffers reportedly put the seats back in their proper positions at daybreak, and fans were unaware of the switch by the time the gates opened for Saturday's game.Navy (3-6) needs to win out this season to reach bowl eligibility under coach Brian Newberry, while Army (5-4) hosts ECU on Saturday in a separate American showdown.
The Army–Navy football rivalry, which airs exclusively on CBS through the 2038 season, dates back to 1890, with the Midshipmen holding a 64-55-7 all-time lead in the series. Navy has won consecutive games against Army, who had won the previous two after the programs alternated wins and losses beginning in 2019.The last on-campus game played between the two came in 2020 in West Point, New York, when the Black Knights blanked the Midshipmen, 15-0.This season's game will be played on Dec. 12 at 3:30 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
Changes coming to Army-Navy gameEarlier this week, the FBS Oversight Committee approved a waiver allowing the historic rivalry game to be played as a 13th contest in the 2027 season coinciding with the adoption of the 24-team playoff.With conference championship games eliminated, this waiver allows Army and Navy to play 12 regular-season games prior to playoff selection day. Then, the two rivals will meet the following weekend to continue one of the greatest traditions in sports while ensuring that the game gets a Saturday to itself."The waiver will also allow Army and Navy to have 12 games, like all other FBS teams, for the College Football Playoff Selection Committee to consider for inclusion into the bracket, followed by a 13th game against each other after playoff selections are made," the committee said in its announcement.
Since 2009, the Black Knights and Midshipmen have played on the second weekend of December to accommodate conference championship weekend, but that changes beginning next season.

title: Titans' Jaylen Harrell hospitalized after serious car accident, remains in hospital in Tampa - CBS Sports
description: The Titans said edge defender Jaylen Harrell remains hospitalized and is receiving care after a serious car accid
body:
The Titans said edge defender Jaylen Harrell remains hospitalized and is receiving care after a serious car accident Friday night in his hometown of Tampa
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:09 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Titans edge defender Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident Friday night in his hometown of Tampa, Fla., and remained hospitalized, the team announced via a statement."Yesterday, Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident that resulted in him being taken to the hospital in his hometown of Tampa, Florida," the statement said. "We have been in constant communication with Jaylen's family and are still working to gather more information. At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate."Harrell, 24, tore his ACL in August and has been on injured reserve ever since, which explains his absence from the team. The Titans visit the Cowboys on Sunday.
A seventh-round pick out of Michigan in 2024, Harrell has spent his entire NFL career with the Titans. He appeared in all 17 games in both 2024 and 2025, contributing on defense and special teams. He had 4.5 sacks last season as well. He is the son of former Lions and Chiefs linebacker James Harrell.

title: Ryan Day buyout, contract details: How much it would cost Ohio State to fire coach after 4th loss in 2026 - CBS Sports
description: Day finds himself under fire again in Columbus after a fourth loss of the season at Nebraska
body:
Day finds himself under fire again in Columbus after a fourth loss of the season at Nebraska
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Ohio State Buckeyes saw their hopes of sneaking into the College Football Playoff snuffed out on Saturday afternoon in Lincoln, Nebraska, as the Huskers snapped a 31-game losing streak to ranked opponents in a 31-28 victory. That loss is the fourth of the season for Ryan Day's Buckeyes, and historically, a four-loss season in Columbus has brought the potential for a coaching change. The last time Ohio State lost four games was 2011, when they went 6-7 in Luke Fickell's lone season in charge before he was replaced by Urban Meyer. Before that, John Cooper was fired after going 8-4 in 2000 and replaced by Jim Tressel. Cooper replaced Earl Bruce in 1988 after Bruce's Buckeyes went 6-4-1. Woody Hayes' last season in charge in Columbus? You guessed it, a 7-4 season. That precedent has to at least concern Day, who has always appeared to be on rocky footing with the Buckeyes after taking over for Urban Meyer. A national title in 2024 calmed down some of the chatter about his job status briefly, but a first-round loss in last year's College Football Playoff and missing out entirely on the 12-team event in 2026 has raised the frustration about Day's performance to a fevered pitch. 
However, if the Buckeyes want to send the coaching carousel into overdrive and open up one of the most coveted jobs in the country, they will have to dig deep into their pockets to cover a massive buyout. Ryan Day buyout, contract details Day has five years remaining on his contract after this year, and instead of being owed a percentage of his remaining salary, his buyout clause calls for him to get paid $11.5 million per year left on his deal. That means after this season, Ohio State would owe Day $57.5 million if it wanted to part ways. That would be the second-largest buyout ever paid, topping the $54 million LSU paid to Brian Kelly last year and the $49 million James Franklin was owed by Penn State -- which ultimately got negotiated down to $9 million. Only Jimbo Fisher's $76 million buyout from Texas A&M would top it, but Ohio State would be near the top of the list of programs that could reasonably handle a $57.5 million buyout if they wanted to.
It will be interesting to see if Day is able to get another year by pointing to the Julian Sayin injury late in the win over Indiana as a good enough reason for their second-half collapse this year. While that is understandably caused offensive issues, the defense taking a step back is perhaps the bigger concern and is harder to explain away. The expectations in Columbus are higher than just about anywhere in the country, but the resources are also better than just about anywhere else either. It's not good enough to simply be in the conversation for a playoff berth, and this will be back-to-back seasons where Day's Buckeyes haven't been at the forefront of the national championship picture. The real question is whether the Buckeyes identify an obviously better candidate to take over for Day. You don't make a $57.5 million coaching firing without having a clear target in mind, and the Buckeyes would have to be confident in their ability to get an upgrade to make the move. 
Perhaps Day's success with the Buckeyes (89-16 record), a coaching market without a clear standout candidate and the cost of his buyout will give him another year to figure things out. But even if he's afforded a chance in 2027, there will be no margin for error granted to him after exhausting his goodwill this season.

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Several teams on the College Football Playoff bubble kept their best-case scenarios in play approaching rivalry weekend to end the regular season.For others, it's all about survival.No. 10 BYU staved off an upset bid at Kansas with a double-overtime win, while No. 14 Ohio State wasn't so lucky after playing itself off the bubble following a loss at Nebraska -- the Huskers' first win under Matt Rhule over a ranked opponent after 10 previous losses.No. 13 Oregon opened Week 12 with its fourth straight win, disposing of Michigan State, 45-7, for style points on Friday night prior to No. 11 Wake Forest's impressive 50-29 victory Saturday afternoon in Atlanta against Georgia Tech. Those are two teams that look the part, with long winning streaks down the stretch.Oregon and Ohio State jumped No. 15 Iowa in this week's third CFP rankings, clearing the Ducks' path to the playoff as the second team out, behind only Texas Tech. The Hawkeyes have one less loss than Oregon this season, but selection committee chair Hunter Yurachek mentioned this week that the Ducks' and Buckeyes' body of work was more impressive.
"First of all, they kind of moved up to a point where we were going to compare the three of them collectively," Yurachek said. "You obviously have some head-to-head in that grouping where Oregon beat Ohio State, Ohio State beat Iowa, and Ohio State obviously had three losses. The strength of schedule for Oregon is nine. For Ohio State, 16. Iowa is 53."CFP bubble entering Saturday's gamesCurrent CFP rankingWeek 12 resultBYUNo. 10Win at Kansas, 31-29 (3OT)Wake ForestNo. 11Win at Georgia Tech, 50-29Texas TechNo. 12at Baylor, 3:30 p.m. ETOregonNo. 13Win at Michigan State, 45-7Ohio StateNo. 14Loss at Nebraska, 31-28Oregon's head-to-head win at Ohio State this season was another data point used by the selection committee this week to rank the bubble teams.From preseason No. 1 to likely falling outside of the top-20 for a second time this season, this has been a campaign to forget for Ryan Day and the Buckeyes. Ohio State fell behind 14 points in the first half at Nebraska and 10 points in the fourth quarter before running out of time in Lincoln.The Buckeyes will finish the season next week against Michigan before likely heading to the Citrus Bowl to face an SEC opponent.Ohio State's loss puts Iowa back in the mix if the Hawkeyes beat Illinois on Saturday. No. 16 Kentucky's path is cloudy coming off back-to-back losses, and the Wildcats are underdogs at Missouri.Expected CFP movement BYU's less-than-impressive win at Kansas means the Cougars could get jumped on Tuesday night by Wake Forest. If the selection committee puts 12th-ranked Texas Tech in the same pod, the Red Raiders may move, too.Texas Tech plays at Baylor on Saturday and needs to win to remain in control of its destiny in the Big 12 Championship race behind Utah. If Kansas had beaten BYU, Texas Tech could've clinched with a win in Waco, but now will have to beat Baylor and TCU (Nov. 26) to get there.If Texas Tech loses at Baylor, Oregon moves up and could get the last-team-in designation on Tuesday night as the final at-large selection.

title: Sacramento Republic end 12-year title drought, outlast Louisville City in 2026 USL Championship final - CBS Sports
description: In front of a packed Heart Health Park crowd, Sacramento defeated Louisville City on penalties to claim its first
body:
In front of a packed Heart Health Park crowd, Sacramento defeated Louisville City on penalties to claim its first USL title since 2014
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:55 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For the first time since 2014, Sacramento Republic are USL Champions. Republic defeated Louisville City FC in a penalty shootout following a 1-1 draw Saturday at Heart Health Park, capturing the club's second title and extending its unbeaten run to 17 matches.In a final between two of the best teams in USL history, it had to have been the narrowest of margins that settled the outcome, with each goalkeeper making a save during the shootout before Sacramento eventually prevailed in front of its home fans.
The second star comes at a symbolic moment for Sacramento Republic, which is preparing to move from Heart Health Park and into a new 20,000-seat soccer-specific venue in the Railyards district of downtown Sacramento in 2028. The emotions were evident on the faces of Louisville City players after the loss as they came to terms with what happened. Despite an early start to the USL Cup final in Sacramento, with kickoff at 9 a.m. local time, there was no need to wait for goals, as Louisville and Sacramento both scored within the opening 32 minutes. Cal Jennings struck in the 14th minute, while Ray Serrano answered in the 31st.
It was then the defenses that took the reins to calm the game down as Sacramento held possession to control a dangerous Louisville attack, and when Evan Davila's shootout attempt hit the post, it opened the door for Sacramento keeper Danny Vitiello to win it, and that he did.An evenly matched final was exactly what many expected, and it delivered for Sacramento fans, who started tailgating at 5:30 a.m. and brought the energy from start to finish. Neil Collins' experienced side looked prepared for the moment, and had Mark-Anthony Kaye's effort not struck the post, Sacramento may have settled the match in regulation. Instead, it required a shootout, and that's where Republic ultimately got the job done.
On the Louisville side, despite winning the Prinx Tires Cup during the regular season, they've now failed to win the final in three appearances since their last triumph in 2018. Considering their regular-season success, they'll want to get over the hump, but given how consistent they've been, it's impossible to say they won't be back at this stage next season.

schema.headline: Sacramento Republic end 12-year title drought, outlast Louisville City in 2026 USL Championship final - CBS Sports

title: Leeds expose Chelsea's unresolved defensive problems as Xabi Alonso's crew yet to find footing - CBS Sports
description: A 4-1 home loss to Leeds laid bare the persistent defensive cracks and tactical chaos that Xabi Alonso has so far
body:
A 4-1 home loss to Leeds laid bare the persistent defensive cracks and tactical chaos that Xabi Alonso has so far failed to fix at Stamford Bridge
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:40 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LONDON -- This was supposed to be the year, the time when Chelsea grew up and a proper manager started extracting consistent performances from a squad whose much-vaunted talent is too rarely expressed in results form. In this most in-flux of Premier League seasons, Xabi Alonso still might leave her with something. It is not going to take particular excellence for a club like this to achieve the bare minimum of Champions League qualification. Adequacy might do it.Once more, however, that is threatening to be a standard beyond Chelsea. This 4-1 defeat at home to old rivals Leeds has them squeezed into the Premier League's middle ground, those above them very visible proof of how much more can be done with less. There is nothing false about that position. Since the last weeks of summer, Alonso's team have given up so much at the back that their likeliest route to success seemed to be supernova seasons from all three of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. Nothing else would paper over the cracks in the defense.And Alonso has tried a lot. Right backs in midfield, center backs as nominal left wing backs that are actually auxiliary central midfielders, switching the right wing back to center forward: in isolation, you could make a case for so many of these adjustments. When the performances are so inconsistent, why not change the XI every game? Alonso's success at Bayer Leverkusen, coupled with the inquisitive footballing mind that made the player so beloved of elite coaches, have earned him the right to experiment. Every change, however, begs the question of what the foundations underlying all this are. Those ought to have shone through this afternoon. Alonso's was as straightforward an XI as he has named. Estevao, Palmer and Rogers off an orthodox center forward, Moises Caicedo running the double pivot and an orthodox back four in front of Emiliano Martinez. This looked like a team intent on playing its way.

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Instead, they had Leeds' game foisted upon them. That might have been different if they had not lost Caicedo. He seemed to have a handle on the game before colliding with James Justin as both competed for a high ball. Those often seemed like the only sort up for grabs today; even when Chelsea played well, they were playing the sort of game Leeds wanted. This wasn't quite the rapid attacking up the gut with which Xabi Alonso charmed the Premier League early in this season. It was bypass the press-ball, get it straight up to the final third and see what comes of it.It can work. Justin, exemplary as a man-marker without the ball and roving agent of chaos in the Chelsea half, cleared a goal kick straight into the back of Morgan Rogers. He moved swiftly up the Leeds gut, his pass to Emmanuel Emegha delivered at just the right moment for the Premier League debutant to slam in the opener. It was perhaps the only moment of clinical execution from the Blues.They needed so many more. After all, this is a team that fails to meet the standards in so many aspects of defending. They press like a newly promoted team. They always seem to name one defender who can be picked on in the duels (starting left back Pep Charravia ranks 101st of 102 defenders for duel success over 300-plus Premier League minutes). Midfielders routinely abandon runners. When Caicedo left this game the feint thread holding the team together was cut.
No one had the composure to deal with the bouncing ball moments after Emegha's opener, Noah Okafor free to move into the box and shoot low through a crowd of legs. No one seemed truly live to the danger for Okafor's second, thundered into the roof of the net when Chelsea could not repel pressure down their right. Between that a contentious penalty, Jayden Bogle's long-range effort striking Rogers right in the grey area between sleeve and arm. If that hadn't been the moment when Chelsea caved, another would have come along."Leeds believed more than us," Alonso admitted. "We didn't show a good enough reaction." The quick one-two punch had been more than enough to send Chelsea heads to the floor. A two-goal deficit ought not to be beyond their reach, but the final 32 minutes saw them outshot seven to six with fewer passes completed into the penalty area. Palmer's most notable action of this game was to row with Joao Pedro as he made his way down the tunnel. Nothing he could have done would have overcome the problems Chelsea made for themselves at the other end. It really wouldn't hurt, though if he did more than nothing.
These feel like problems unresolved by a manager who was supposed to be the savior. Eleven Premier League games is not a lot to turn the tide but it is enough to give us a sense of who this team are. The answer is a team whose early scoring streak covered for a below-average attack (1.25 non-penalty expected goals per game, 14th in the Premier League) and a below-average defense (1.44 non-penalty expected goals allowed per game, 15th in the Premier League). The game state-warping impact of scoring with your first shot can only mitigate so much.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Is it time for a conversation about Alonso and pressure? If so it has to be caveated by the unity and purpose he fostered at Bayer Leverkusen, qualities this dressing room sorely needs. He might not have corralled the superstars at Real Madrid but the press and possession system he forged could have achieved great things given time. Stitching together a version of this Chelsea, overloaded with number 10s and underpowered defensive players, that suits the more direct and chaotic Premier League was always going to be a coaching challenge.And of course this is not the Roman Abramovich era. Swapping out coaches is not a silver bullet for perennial trophy contenders but instead the modus operandi of an ownership group that are the most serious problem at Stamford Bridge. Someone is going to have to be afforded time to corral this squad or indeed tear it down and start again. Doing that is going to be a club-wide effort, including fans. Few of them hung around to wave off a side who had allowed old rivals Leeds a first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999, the same side who had let Tottenham break the habit of a lifetime last month.
The vibes are bad. The performances might be worse. This brand new start is feeling all too familiar.

schema.headline: Leeds expose Chelsea's unresolved defensive problems as Xabi Alonso's crew yet to find footing - CBS Sports
